solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: They go round back of French passes

indicators.note: back tells us to turn the French word round so it reads the other way

parts.note: de is the French word for of
to pass away is to die, so passes means dies

explanation.surface: A traveller notes the switchbacks of mountain passes at the far end of France.
explanation.definitionFit: Eddies are swirling currents of water or air, things that circle as they move.

clue.text: Tight tie tangled with beard

indicators.note: a tangle mixes things up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tie caught up in a man's beard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tight' looks like it describes the tie, but it means drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebriated is a rare word for drunk, and tight is slang for drunk.

clue.text: Hinder harangue about Italy in decline

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the two words go round Italy's letter

parts.note: to deter is to hinder or discourage
to orate is to speak pompously, to harangue
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: Holding back a rant about Italy's decline.
explanation.definitionFit: To deteriorate is to decline or grow worse, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Busy with small, stolen glance

parts.note: busy and eye are both British slang for a detective or police officer
hot means stolen, as in hot goods

explanation.surface: A busy person snatches a quick look at something small and stolen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Busy' is British slang for a police officer; so is 'eye', as in private eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeshot is an old word for a glance, as well as the range of one's sight.

clue.text: Adult drug shaped like a star

parts.note: A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult
a steroid is a drug, often a performance-enhancing one

explanation.surface: An adult drug comes in a star-shaped pill.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective asteroid means star-shaped, from Greek aster, a star; starfish are called asteroids.

clue.text: Animal is singular — exactly!

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
to a T means exactly or perfectly

explanation.surface: Someone insists, emphatically, that an animal is unique.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoat is a small animal of the weasel family, the ermine in winter.

clue.text: Soft porn books stashed by Heather

indicators.note: stashed by means the books are hidden within the heather

parts.note: Erica is the botanical name of heather, and a girl's name
OT, the Old Testament, is the crossword abbreviation for books

explanation.surface: Heather has hidden a pile of racy books.
explanation.definitionFit: Erotica is sexually arousing literature or art, short of hardcore pornography.

clue.text: Heads of international boxing organisation held up belt

indicators.note: in a down clue held up means read from the bottom, so the letters go backwards
heads of means the first letter of each word

explanation.surface: Boxing officials hold up the championship belt.
explanation.walkthrough: The heads spell IBO, itself a real boxing body, which makes it easy to miss the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: An obi is the broad sash worn with a kimono, a kind of belt.

clue.text: Teacher caught in act scratching bottom itch

indicators.note: caught in says the teacher is trapped inside the other word
scratching out the bottom removes the last letter in a down clue

parts.note: a deed is an act
sir is what pupils call a male teacher

explanation.surface: A teacher is caught scratching an itchy backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'itch' looks like part of the joke, but it is the definition, as in an itch to travel.
explanation.definitionFit: An itch for something is a craving, a strong desire.

clue.text: In discussion, still interrupting Eeyore — sadly, that's not right

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking in, so the word for still goes inside
sadly, fitting gloomy Eeyore, signals that the letters are rearranged
not right means R, for right, is taken out

parts.note: still means yet, as in still to come

explanation.surface: Someone chips in on Eeyore's mournful remarks, insisting he is mistaken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' fits gloomy Eeyore, which hides that it is the anagram signal; the leftover letters are reordered as E…OEYE around the inserted word.
explanation.definitionFit: Talking eye to eye means face to face, directly in conversation.

clue.text: Renegade filibuster stripped of his external prize

indicators.note: the pirate loses the letters lying on his outside, at both ends, which together spell the prize

parts.note: in its old sense a filibuster is a freebooter, a pirate
a pie is a classic prize, as at a fair or a pie-eating contest

explanation.surface: A long-winded politician is stripped of an award he won abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Filibuster' suggests endless speeches, but here it is its older sense, a pirate. The PIE taken away is split around what is left: P-I at the front and E at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat is someone who deserts or betrays their side, the same as a renegade.

clue.text: Original meanings of old record in English stymie novel

indicators.note: in places the old record inside the reworked letters
novel means new, so the letters are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: a log is a written record, as in a ship's log

explanation.surface: An old document in English baffles a novelist with its original senses of words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book beside 'record', but it is the anagram signal; 'in' puts OLOG into TYMIES, the rearranged STYMIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Etymologies are the histories of words, tracing them back to their earliest senses.

clue.text: It doesn't collide with ball bearing, ruined

parts.note: a person's air is their bearing or manner
shot means worn out or ruined, as in nerves being shot

explanation.surface: A ball bearing that has been wrecked no longer collides properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ball bearing' reads as one machine part, but 'ball' belongs to the definition and 'bearing' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf or cricket an air shot is a swing that misses the ball completely.

clue.text: Perhaps from which we'd find rain hit unexpectedly?

definitions.text: Perhaps from which we'd find rain hit unexpectedly?

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests the letters arrive in a surprise order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sudden downpour seems to come from nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: something arriving out of the blue comes 'out of thin air', just as sudden rain might.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that appear unexpectedly are said to come out of thin air, from nowhere at all.

clue.text: Playing Gaelic harp on Love Island series?

indicators.note: on means placed after, below in a down entry
playing suggests the letters are moved around freely

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: Someone plays a Celtic harp on the reality show Love Island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love Island' is a British reality dating show, which hides the split: 'Love' is O and 'Island series' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An archipelago is a chain of islands, a series of them.

clue.text: Entering Egypt, stole old enemy vessel

indicators.note: entering says the stole goes into the letters for Egypt

parts.note: ET is the international vehicle code for Egypt
a boa is a long scarf or stole of feathers or fur

explanation.surface: Someone sneaks into Egypt and steals an old enemy ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stole' looks like a past-tense verb but is the noun, a scarf.
explanation.definitionFit: An E-boat was a fast German torpedo boat of the Second World War, a British foe.

clue.text: European weapon for fencing maybe Polish?

indicators.note: fencing means enclosing, so the weapon surrounds the next piece

parts.note: a lance is a long weapon carried by a mounted knight
eg, for example, is what 'maybe' signals: one possible case

explanation.surface: A European weapon used in fencing, perhaps one from Poland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the nationality, but it is the noun meaning refinement; 'fencing' is not the sport but enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: Polish in the sense of refined style or sophistication is the same as elegance.

clue.text: Catholic, Celtic accent essentially jarred

indicators.note: jarred means jolted, so the letters are shaken into a new order
essentially means at its heart, the middle letters of the word

explanation.surface: A Catholic with a Celtic accent sounds jarring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catholic' is not the faith; with a small c it means wide-ranging, and capitalised at the start it hides that.
explanation.definitionFit: Catholic tastes are broad and universal, drawing on many sources, which is what eclectic means.

clue.text: Widest minor route is in Paris

parts.note: a B road is a British minor road, below an A road
est is French for is

explanation.surface: The widest minor road is found in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: British roads are graded: A roads are major, B roads minor.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadest and widest are both superlatives meaning of the greatest width.

clue.text: Clan member cutting lines on most of tree trunk

indicators.note: cutting into means the member is put inside the trunk
most of means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a caber is the tree trunk tossed at Scottish Highland games
MP stands for Member of Parliament
L is the abbreviation for line, so LL is lines

explanation.surface: A clansman is cutting lines into most of a tree trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clan member' reads as one definition, but only 'Clan' defines; the caber is the trunk tossed at Scottish Highland games.
explanation.definitionFit: The Campbells are one of the great Scottish Highland clans.

clue.text: Fanciful charge for peeping Lords, at least

definitions.text: Fanciful charge for peeping Lords, at least

parts.words: Fanciful charge for peeping Lords, at least
parts.note: a peer can be one who peeps or a lord; read whimsically, the word is a fee for peering, as postage is a fee for posting, while really meaning the nobility

explanation.surface: A whimsical fee for looking, charged to the House of Lords at the very least.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fanciful' warns that the -age ending is being read as a charge, like postage; the real sense is the body of peers.
explanation.definitionFit: The peerage is the nobility as a whole, of which the Lords are at least a part.

clue.text: Willow's more promising when pollarded

indicators.note: pollarding cuts the top off a tree, so the first letter goes

parts.note: rosier prospects are more promising ones

explanation.surface: A willow tree looks healthier after its crown is cut back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pollarded' fits the tree surface perfectly, which hides that it is the top-removal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The osier is a species of willow whose flexible shoots are used in basket-making.

clue.text: Bound dictionary, unusually glib inside

indicators.note: inside places the rearranged letters within the dictionary

parts.note: the OED is the Oxford English Dictionary

indicators.note: unusually means not in the normal order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bound dictionary with oddly glib entries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' looks like it describes the book, but it is the definition, as in duty-bound.
explanation.definitionFit: To be bound to do something is to be obliged, compelled by duty or law.

clue.text: Nearly pick out cheated mercenary

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to sort is to pick out or select
to do someone is to cheat them, so did means cheated

explanation.surface: A mercenary is singled out for nearly cheating.
explanation.definitionFit: Sordid can mean motivated by greed or base self-interest, as in sordid gain.

clue.text: Stuff to burn after husband's done a bunk

indicators.note: doing a bunk is British slang for running away, so the husband leaves

parts.note: to overheat is to get so hot one burns

explanation.surface: Left to burn the dinner after her husband ran off.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'do a bunk' is British slang for running off.
explanation.definitionFit: To stuff yourself is to eat far too much, which is to overeat.

clue.text: United Artists holding up commerce

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters read from bottom to top
holding means the words contain the answer within them

explanation.surface: A film studio stalls its business dealings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' finds EDART across unitED ARTists, and 'up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Trade is buying and selling goods, the same as commerce.

clue.text: About to check tree in crater

indicators.note: to check is to hold back, so the word for about holds the tree inside it

parts.note: ca, circa, means about
the alder is a tree of damp ground

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to inspect a tree growing in a crater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'check' suggests inspecting, but it means restrain: CA holds ALDER.
explanation.definitionFit: A caldera is a large volcanic crater formed when a volcano collapses.

clue.text: Identify round spring linked to furious knocking

indicators.note: round means turned about, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: to ID someone is to identify them
a spa is a mineral spring
raging means furious

explanation.surface: Spotting a spring connected with furious hammering.
explanation.definitionFit: Knocking, in the sense of criticising harshly, means the same as disparaging.

clue.text: Worthy men led my son — all may follow this great wave

definitions.text: Worthy men led my son — all may follow this
definitions.meaning: every one of the six words can follow the answer: seaworthy, seamen, sealed, seamy, season, seawall
a ... is a large heavy wave, as in a ship being struck by a ...

explanation.surface: Good sailors guided a son across ocean swells.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors call a single large breaking wave a sea, as in shipping a heavy sea.

clue.text: Put away hater, saving skin

indicators.note: saving skin means keeping what is inside once the outer letters are peeled off

explanation.surface: Someone hateful is jailed, but escapes a beating.
explanation.definitionFit: To put away food is to eat it, and ate is that action in the past tense.

clue.text: Disease makes most of beasts die, sadly

indicators.note: sadly suggests the letters are in a sorry state, so they are rearranged
most of drops the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: An illness that kills most animals, regrettably.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims BEASTS to BEAST, which with DIE is shuffled by 'sadly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Diabetes is a chronic illness in which the body cannot regulate blood sugar.

clue.text: Ingenious answer, right?

parts.note: droit is a right in law, from the French

explanation.surface: Is that a clever answer?
explanation.definitionFit: Adroit means skilful and quick-witted, much the same as ingenious.
